Sup-t simultaneous confidence bands for impulse responses

Source: R/lp-joint.R
lp_supt.Rd

Montiel Olea & Plagborg-Moller (2019) sup-t bands. With \(\hat\sigma_h\) the standard error of \(\hat\beta_h\) and \(\hat R\) the correlation matrix implied by the joint covariance, the band is $$\hat\beta_h \pm \hat c_{1-\alpha}\hat\sigma_h,\qquad \hat c_{1-\alpha} = (1-\alpha)\text{-quantile of } \max_h |z_h|,\ z\sim N(0,\hat R),$$ computed by simulation. The band covers the entire response path with probability \(1-\alpha\) (asymptotically), is narrower than Bonferroni and is never narrower than the pointwise band.

Usage

lp_supt(object, level = 0.9, nsim = 10000L, seed = NULL)

Arguments

object

an object with a $vcov element: lp_joint(), lp_smooth() or lp_panel().

level

simultaneous coverage level.

nsim

number of simulation draws.

seed

optional RNG seed.

Value

a tibble with columns response, horizon, estimate, std.error, pw_low, pw_high (pointwise at level), conf.low, conf.high (sup-t); the critical values are in attr(, "crit"). tidy() stacks the two band types and autoplot() compares them.

Details

Economic intuition. A pointwise 90% band is a statement about one horizon at a time; across 20 horizons the chance that the true path leaves it somewhere is far above 10%. Use sup-t bands when you want to claim that a whole shape (a hump, a sign, "no response at any horizon") is supported. Because LP estimates are strongly positively correlated across horizons the sup-t critical value is usually only modestly above 1.64 (typically 2.0-2.5), not the 3+ of Bonferroni. Pitfall: it needs a good joint covariance (heavy persistence makes HAC covariances unreliable at long horizons) and horizons with zero variance (normalised impact) are ignored.

See also

Other local projections: autoplot.lpm(), compare_lp_var(), lp(), lp_forecast(), lp_joint(), lp_panel(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

fit <- lp_joint(yraw, shock = rate, horizon = 8, lags = 2, contemp = c(infl, unemp))
b <- lp_supt(fit, level = 0.9, seed = 1)
attr(b, "crit")
#>     infl    unemp     rate 
#> 2.251103 2.323445 2.267141
